summary: Friday 10-30 is dominated by macro and crypto, not single-name news. A record Binance hack (about $6.3B) pushed BTC to about $77k, and the AI-capex selloff widened (Alphabet about -12% on 10-29, Amazon about -7% and Intel sliding on Q3 prints) on top of a hawkish Fed hold (two hike dissents, Polymarket 82% December hike). The next hard single-name events are Monday 11-02 (CLX and IDXX, plus a likely but unverified AAPL print) and a cluster on 11-03 to 11-05. Earnings distances below are trading days (10-30 is a Friday), so 11-05 is 4 trading days out and 11-06 is the 5-day edge. The file's days_to_earnings counts calendar days. The 10-29 earnings wave (HWM, LNG, INCY, BDC, EXEL, CART) is resolved from filings, and no 8-K 4.01 or 4.02 appears anywhere. Learning: L2 shaped this note (every symbol in the inputs is covered, with dates checked against filings); L1, L3 and L4 do not apply to this role. My own high-event-risk flags grade at about 52% over 40 calls, so they mark variance, not direction.

Binance suffered what Benzinga calls the biggest crypto hack on record (about $6.3B, 10-29), and BTC fell about 3% to about $77k. The hack reportedly involved borrowing Ether against stablecoins. Trezor separately reported a suspected hardware implant in one of its devices. Analysts name $76.3k and $73k as support and one warns of a final Q4 selloff. Binance's solvency and any withdrawal limits are not covered in these headlines. Other pressure: a hawkish Fed (82% December hike odds), a hot-PCE selloff warning from Cowen, and the CLARITY Act at risk of midterm gridlock (O'Leary). Strategy (MSTR) reported Q3 on 10-29; Saylor said it does not need BTC or equity issuance to do the heavy lifting, and the stock is down 44% on the year. Constructive but non-binding: Hagerty on a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve, Google's crypto custody platform. Quantum-risk, Polymarket politics and price-target items are opinion.

The AI-capex worry flagged since 10-20 now has hard facts. Alphabet lost about $482B (about -12% on 10-29), Amazon fell more than 7% despite 39% AWS growth on $220B of AI spending and an earnings miss, and Intel slid on a deepening PC slump and memory shortages (Dell about -10%). Value beat the S&P by 4.2 points in October, the widest gap since 2001. Futures were mixed this morning. Hawkish-Fed backdrop: Trump says inflation is 'way down' while Chair Warsh says prices remain too high.

notable.headline: Binance $6.3B hack; Bitcoin drops to $77,000 (also 'holds $77,000' and a Trezor hardware-tampering alert)
notable.read: The one hard crypto event of the day: the largest exchange hack on record. BTC fell only about 3%, which says the market is treating it as contained so far. Watch for Binance withdrawal limits or solvency statements, which are not in these headlines. Continues the contested-$80k thread from 10-27 to 10-29, and the break below $80k has now happened.
